studyScope: Historical 2023 proposal and 2024 Phase 3 final action; no assertion about currently operative regulations.
selection: Two purposively selected requests with explicit named responses in section 2.5 of EPA's response document. Selected after reading responses; not a random sample, complete section census or docket denominator.
sourceAuthentication: Public API metadata projections and page-scoped visual review of downloaded official PDFs. Offline fingerprints check saved consistency, not independent authentication of the original source bytes or correctness of the coding.

responseDocument.title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles: Phase 3, Response to Comments
responseDocument.reviewScope: Introduction/methodology and specified request/response pages only; not a manual review of all 2114 pages.
responseDocument.excerptScope: EPA describes selected technical comments as reproduced verbatim in excerpts. Responses can address multiple commenters and are not limited to immediately preceding excerpts. Repeated excerpts are not independent submissions.
responseDocument.chronologyCaveat: Printed page 2 refers to comments after July 18, 2024 despite the March 2024 document date. Retained as an apparent source inconsistency, not silently corrected or used as an eligibility cutoff.
responseDocument.priorityCaveat: The introduction identifies the final-rule preamble as definitive if inconsistent with the response document. The docket also contains a separately finalized locomotive-preemption rule.

final.reviewScope: Amendatory instruction 103; 40 CFR 1037.705(b) equation and Std definition only.

correction.reviewScope: EPA summary and publication-error explanations only. The preceding VA text on PDF page 1 is not this rule.

regulatoryComparison.interpretation: The final definition omits the proposed additional MY2027+ zero-CO2 vocational common-reference sentence. EPA explains a collective change to its standard-setting approach and separately clarifies continued tractor credit eligibility. Neither the text difference nor the collective response identifies a single comment's causal effect.
regulatoryComparison.correctionBoundary: The June 2024 correction addresses errors in preparing the final rule for publication, including a tractor/vocational table substitution. It is a separate event from Allison's allegation about the proposed NPRM calculation.

attributes.title: Comment
Comment submitted by Allison Transmission, Inc.

reviews.requestSummary: Clarify that the credit equation applies to tractors as well as vocational vehicles despite the proposed zero-tailpipe-CO2 provision's reference to vocational standards.
reviews.responseAnchor: In response to Cummins, we clarify that manufacturers can continue
reviews.responseSummary: EPA explicitly clarifies that manufacturers can continue using the equation for tractor CO2 credits; the proposed vocational common-reference update was not intended to exclude tractors.
reviews.claimBoundary: Documented clarification, not newly granted tractor eligibility or an identified causal rule change attributable to Cummins.

reviews.requestSummary: Correct allegedly erroneous calculations in five of six proposed LHD vocational standards. EPA's excerpt cites original page 2 and refers to an unread appendix on pages 4-5.
reviews.responseAnchor: we disagree that there was an error in the NPRM
reviews.responseSummary: EPA explicitly disagrees with the alleged NPRM error and says Allison misunderstood its method. It separately changed the broader method after considering collective concerns.
reviews.claimBoundary: Rejection of the specific error claim, not a conclusion that Allison had no influence. Neither the collective method change nor the later publication correction proves acceptance of this claim.
